options.text: The ball falls with constant acceleration.
The ball falls with constant speed.
The ball falls with decreasing speed.
The ball falls with increasing acceleration.

The table shows readings of the gas pressure inside the bubble and the volume of the bubble.
The temperature of the water in the lake is constant.
The values in three rows of the table are correct and one row is not correct.
Which row is not correct?
pressure/kPa volume/cm3

glass tube
mercury
air

options.text: expansion of air in the flask
expansion of the glass flask
expansion of the glass tube
expansion of the mercury

questions.questionText:

P Q
brass copper
silver iron
S R
Wax is used to attach small metal balls at the rod ends P, Q, R and S.
Each rod is the same size. They are heated uniformly by a Bunsen burner at point X.
As the rods warm up, the wax melts and the balls fall off.
Why does the ball on the silver rod fall first?

options.text: Silver is the best conductor of heat.
Silver is the worst conductor of heat.
Silver is the best radiator of heat.
Silver is the worst radiator of heat.

real or virtual distance of the image from the mirror

real the same distance from the mirror as the object
virtual closer to the mirror than the object
virtual the same distance from the mirror as the object

I O
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The image I is diminished.
The image I is inverted.
The image I is real.
The object O is closer to the lens than its principal focus.

20kHz–150kHz

questions.questionText:
A positively charged balloon is placed against a wall. The charge makes the balloon stick to the
wall.
Which statement explains this?

options.text: Positive charges on the balloon attract electrons in the wall.
Positive charges on the balloon attract protons in the wall.
Positive charges on the balloon repel electrons in the wall.
Positive charges on the balloon repel protons in the wall.

A student is trying to determine the resistance of a lamp. He sets up the incorrect circuit shown.
V A
Which change would allow him to take the measurements needed to calculate the resistance of
the lamp?

options.text: Disconnect the ammeter and move it to the left of the lamp.
Swap the positions of the ammeter and the voltmeter in the circuit.
Disconnect the ammeter and connect it in parallel with the lamp.
Disconnect the voltmeter and connect it in parallel with the lamp.

questions.questionText:
When a thin gold foil is bombarded with alpha particles, some alpha particles are deflected
through large angles.
Which statement explains this deflection?

options.text: Most of the atom consists of empty space.
All of the positive charge and most of the mass of the gold atom are concentrated in a small volume.
Positive charge in the gold atom is spread evenly throughout the atom.
All of the negative charge is concentrated at its centre.

questions.questionText:
A detector near a radioactive source shows a reading of 2000 counts/minute.
How is the corrected count rate determined?

options.text: by moving the detector closer to the source
by placing an absorber between the detector and the source
by repeating and averaging the measurements
by taking away the background radiation count rate

questions.questionText: Which statement about alpha, beta and gamma radiation is not correct?

options.text: Alpha particles are deflected most in an electric field.
Beta particles are deflected most in a magnetic field.
Gamma radiation is not deflected by a magnetic field.
Gamma radiation is least ionising.

questions.questionText:
A sample of a radioactive material has a half-life of 20 minutes.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: After 30 minutes, less than half of the material has decayed.
After 40 minutes, all of the radioactive material has decayed.
After 60 minutes, an eighth of the radioactive material remains.
After 120 minutes, a sixth of the radioactive material remains.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.text: The Earth orbits the Sun once in approximately 24 hours.
The Earth orbits the Moon once in approximately 1 week.
The Moon orbits the Earth once in approximately 1 month.
The Sun orbits the Earth once in approximately 365 days.

questions.questionText:
Stars are powered by nuclear reactions that release energy.
Which statement describes the nuclear reaction in stable stars?

options.text: Nuclear fission converts helium into hydrogen.
Nuclear fission converts hydrogen into helium.
Nuclear fusion converts helium into hydrogen.
Nuclear fusion converts hydrogen into helium.
